findings.summary: role=img is set on the Leaflet map root, which is also a keyboard stop and the parent of the attribution links.
findings.fix: Put role=img and the text alternative on a non-interactive wrapper. Leave the Leaflet container without that role so its tabindex and the Leaflet, OpenStreetMap, CARTO, Privacy, and Terms links stay exposed as links.
findings.evidence: connect() calls L.map(this.canvasTarget), then setAttribute("role","img"). attributionPrefix() and CARTO_ATTRIBUTION inject links into that same node. Leaflet 1.9 defaults keyboard to true, which sets tabindex=0 on the container.

findings.summary: Closing map search or map settings hides the focused control and does not return focus to the button that opened it.
findings.fix: In closeMobileSearch, focus the Search stations button before hiding the overlay. In closeSettings, focus the Map settings button before hiding the panel. Escape already calls both methods.
findings.evidence: openMobileSearch focuses the search input inside the overlay. closeMobileSearch and closeSettings only set hidden. closeSettings updates aria-expanded. Neither method calls focus() on the opener.

findings.summary: The map Search stations button opens an overlay but exposes no expanded state and names no controlled panel.
findings.fix: Give the mobile search container an id. Set aria-expanded and aria-controls on the button, and update aria-expanded in openMobileSearch and closeMobileSearch, the same way the Map settings button does.
findings.evidence: The button has only aria-label="Search stations". The settings button in maps/show.html.erb sets aria-expanded and aria-controls="map-settings-panel".

notes: Automated setup. This pass did not run axe. Scan http://127.0.0.1:3000 after bin/dev (Procfile.dev starts Puma, the esbuild watcher, and the Tailwind watcher). Leave https://waterlevels.org out of headless runs; Cloudflare Turnstile blocks them. Keep the current static checks and add one browser runner. Gemfile has no Capybara, Selenium, or Cuprite. package.json has no Playwright, Cypress, Jest, or Pa11y, and yarn test:js is node --test with no DOM. Use Playwright with @axe-core/playwright. Cypress, Jest, and Storybook would be a second stack this app does not have. Pa11y standards are WCAG2A, WCAG2AA, and WCAG2AAA, with no WCAG 2.2 tag. Run axe with tags wcag2a, wcag2aa, wcag21a, wcag21aa, and wcag22aa. axe-core covers one new WCAG 2.2 criterion, 2.5.8 Target Size (rule target-size). 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured, 2.5.7 Dragging Movements, 3.2.6 Consistent Help, 3.3.7 Redundant Entry, and 3.3.8 Accessible Authentication stay manual. A Lighthouse accessibility score of 100 is a subset of axe and is not conformance. Automation misses accurate names, tab order, focus return, live-region timing, and custom keyboard behavior.

Automated cases. On load, scan /, /map, /alerts, /gauges/wa, one gauge URL, /about, /faq, /contact, /subscriptions when alerts are enabled (the controller returns 404 when they are off), /privacy, /terms, /disclosures, and /aup. Scan again after interaction, limited to the changed region: open the mobile menu; open one FAQ answer; type two characters in the home combobox and wait for #home-search-results; below 768px open map search and wait for #map-search-results; open #map-settings-panel; deny geolocation and wait for [role=dialog]; POST the contact form empty and scan the 422 page; on /gauges/wa clear a measurement checkbox and wait for the status text; on /alerts clear a flood-stage checkbox. Include .map-canvas so its accessible name is checked. Until role=img moves off the Leaflet root, expect nested interactive or hidden-link failures there. Seed a few Washington stations, including one in major flood (demo site 99000020). Skip the full 864k-row db:seed on every pull request. The smoke test never requests /gauges/wa or /subscriptions, and the test named keyboard-accessible only searches the HTML string. Extend that Minitest file for static strings: skip link, filter group labels, the subscription email label, and flood status text such as Major Flooding. Keep those string checks separate from any keyboard assertion. Filter checkboxes are size-4 (16px) inside a full-width label in states.css .filter-check and in the map layer labels. When axe reports target-size, measure the label row. WCAG 2.5.8 allows a target under 24 CSS pixels when the 24px circles around adjacent targets do not overlap. Map close buttons are size-8 and size-10.

Manual keyboard checklist. Unplug the mouse. Cover /, /map, /faq, /contact, /gauges/wa, /alerts, and /subscriptions, and use the skip link on /about, /privacy, /terms, /disclosures, and /aup. Test the mobile menu and map search at 375px. At the md breakpoint (768px) .header-actions and .map-mobile-search are display:none, and .desktop-nav is shown. Keys: Tab and Shift+Tab move between controls; Enter activates a link or button; Space activates a button or toggles a checkbox; Escape closes an overlay; Arrow keys move inside a combobox; Home and End are optional in a list. The only acceptable trap is the geolocation dialog, and Escape must leave it. WCAG 2.1.1, 2.4.1, 2.4.3, 2.4.7, 2.4.11, and 1.4.11.

Keyboard, skip link and mobile nav. First Tab on every page is Skip to main content (app/views/layouts/application.html.erb). It sits off-screen until focus (.skip-link uses translateY(-200%) and returns on :focus and :focus-visible, with a white outline). Enter moves focus to #main. Shift+Tab from the first control in main reaches the skip link again. Below 768px, the menu button name is Open main menu, aria-expanded is false, and aria-controls is mobile-primary-nav. Enter or Space opens it, focus moves to the first link, and the name becomes Close main menu with aria-expanded true. Tab through Map, Flood Alerts, About, FAQ, Contact, Data, and Manage Email Alerts when alerts are on. The panel is a disclosure, so Tab must be able to leave it. Escape closes it and returns focus to the toggle (mobile_nav_controller.js). At 768px and wider, those buttons are display:none and the desktop links in nav Primary are the tab stops, with aria-current=page on the current item. Confirm the focus ring is the global cyan 2px outline and is not fully covered by the header (2.4.11).

Keyboard, FAQ and comboboxes. On /faq, category controls are buttons in nav FAQ categories. Enter or Space shows that section and sets aria-current=true on the active button. Arrow keys between categories are optional. Each question is a button in an h3 with aria-expanded and aria-controls. Enter or Space toggles it. Opening one closes the others. The answer is a region named by the question. Up and Down between headers are optional in the APG accordion pattern. A hash such as /faq#id opens that item and must not trap focus. Home combobox: the input name is Search stations, role=combobox, aria-expanded starts false, aria-controls=home-search-results. After two characters the listbox opens, aria-expanded becomes true, and the polite status says N results available or No matching stations. Down and Up set aria-activedescendant and aria-selected. Enter follows the active option. Enter with no active option goes to the first result or /map. Escape closes the list, clears the active descendant, and leaves focus in the input. Tab must not stick in the list. Options are links, so if Tab enters them the accessible name is the station, state, or ZIP. Use my location is a button; while it works it is disabled and aria-busy=true. Map combobox (#map-search-input, #map-search-results) follows the same APG combobox pattern. Arrow keys run from the document keydown listener only while that input is focused and the list is open, so test arrows there. The combobox and its Search stations button exist below 768px. At desktop width they are display:none; use Stations in view for the same task.

Keyboard, map canvas, settings, and geolocation dialog. After load, the canvas name is Water gauges map. Use Search stations or the Stations in view list for keyboard access. Markers are not required tab stops (2.1.1 equivalent path: search, Stations in view, /gauges/wa, /alerts, and gauge pages). Dragging the map is not the only way to reach a station (2.5.7). Zoom in, Zoom out, Use my location, and Map settings are buttons outside the canvas and stay in tab order with a visible ring. Tab to the attribution links (Leaflet, WaterLevels.org, Privacy, Terms, OpenStreetMap, CARTO) and record whether they are announced. They currently sit inside the role=img node. Map settings: the button starts aria-expanded=false and aria-controls=map-settings-panel. Enter or Space opens the panel and sets aria-expanded=true. Tab reaches Close settings, the Measurement filters checkboxes, the Station status checkbox, and the station links. Space toggles a checkbox. Escape and Close settings hide the panel. Focus must return to Map settings. closeSettings does not do that when focus is inside the panel. The panel is a disclosure, so a focus trap is not required, and the zoom buttons may stay tabbable if the ring stays visible (2.4.11). Below 768px, Search stations opens the full-screen overlay and focuses #map-search-input. The button currently has no aria-expanded or aria-controls. Run the combobox checks, then Close search and Escape. Focus must return to Search stations. closeMobileSearch does not call focus(). While the overlay is open, map chrome is display:none; confirm Tab does not land under it. Geolocation dialog, from home and from the map, after denying permission, timing out, or with geolocation missing: role=dialog, aria-modal=true, title and body match the error (Location permission denied, Location request timed out, Location not supported, or Couldn't get your location). Focus lands on OK. Tab and Shift+Tab cycle only through Close and OK. Escape, OK, Close, and the backdrop close it and restore focus to the locate button. Also check 200% zoom and a 320px width on the map chrome, FAQ, and both forms (1.4.4, 1.4.10). prefers-reduced-motion is already in the CSS; confirm the menu and FAQ do not depend on motion.

Keyboard, forms, state directory, and flood status. Contact (/contact): tab order is Name, Email address, Subject, Your message, the Turnstile widget when it renders, then Send message. Each control has a visible label (1.3.1, 3.3.2, 2.5.3). The placeholder is a hint. Submit empty and with email bad. The response is 422. Each invalid field has aria-invalid=true and aria-describedby pointing at contact-name-error, contact-email-error, contact-subject-error, or contact-message-error, and the error text is visible (3.3.1). The form does a full page render (data-turbo=false); confirm focus is findable on the first error (2.4.3). A Turnstile failure exposes role=alert on #contact-turnstile-error. Email hello@waterlevels.org works without solving the widget (3.3.8). The honeypot subtitle is not a tab stop. Subscriptions (/subscriptions, alerts enabled): the email field label is Email address, for=manage-link-email, autocomplete=email, required. The submit button is Email me a manage link. When TURNSTILE_SECRET is set, the widget is named Bot check and is reachable. A failed check shows a role=alert flash, Please complete the bot check and try again, and the email value remains (3.3.1, 3.3.7). Success is a role=status notice, If that address is subscribed, a manage link is on its way. The honeypot is not a tab stop. State directory (/gauges/wa): Search stations has a visible label. Groups are Measurement types (Streamflow, Gauge Height, Water Quality and Temp), Station status when any station is stale (Show offline / stale), and Flood alerts when any station is in flood (Stations with alerts). Space toggles the native checkboxes. The polite live region becomes N stations shown or No stations match these filters, once (4.1.3). Hidden cards are not in the tab order. Quick county jump is a details/summary; Enter or Space opens it; the links are real hrefs to the county headings. At 1024px and wider the details starts open. Flood-stage checkboxes are on /alerts, where the same component groups by state: Action Stage, Minor Flooding, Moderate Flooding, and Major Flooding, plus Measurement types and Quick state jump. /alerts does not render the Stations with alerts checkbox. Flood status (1.4.1, 1.4.3, 1.4.11): turn on grayscale or a color-vision simulation. Map legend text is Normal (circle), Action (A / diamond), Minor (1 / square), Moderate (2 / triangle), Major (3 / triangle), and Inactive (x). The swatches are aria-hidden. On /gauges/wa and /alerts the status words are Major Flooding, Moderate Flooding, Minor Flooding, Action Stage, Nominal, or Offline, and the dot is aria-hidden. Demo site 99000020 is major flood. The CSS token test only bans text-zinc-500 in stylesheets, so check the rendered flood red, rose, and orange on zinc-950, and the legend labels in text-zinc-400. Help (Contact in the primary nav, and hello@waterlevels.org on the contact page) should sit in the same place on all 12 pages (3.2.6).

Screen reader guide. Minimum pair: NVDA with Chrome or Firefox, and VoiceOver with Safari. Add JAWS with Chrome for an enterprise pass, and VoiceOver on iOS for the mobile menu and the map search overlay. WebAIM Screen Reader User Survey #11 (July-August 2026) is a survey sample, not market share. Set NVDA speech near 40 percent while learning, and turn on browse-mode auto focus. NVDA key is Insert, or Caps Lock if set. Stop speech with Ctrl. Down and Up read items. H and Shift+H move by heading. D moves by landmark. F moves by form field. B moves by button. NVDA+F7 lists headings, links, and landmarks. Enter activates. Enter on a field enters forms mode; Escape leaves it. VoiceOver: Cmd+F5 toggles. VO is Control+Option. VO+Right and VO+Left move. VO+Space activates. VO+U opens the rotor (headings, landmarks, form controls, links). On iOS, swipe through a station card and a search result. The status word and the value stay separate words, and the hidden dot is not an empty stop.

Screen reader, page skeleton and the listed components. On each of the 12 pages: the title is announced (2.4.2); the rotor shows one h1 and no skipped levels (1.3.1, 2.4.6); landmarks include a banner, a nav named Primary, main, and a content info. FAQ also has a nav named FAQ categories. The map main is the map. Skip to main content is a link before the banner, and activating it lands in main. Mobile menu button announces Open main menu, collapsed. After activation it announces Close main menu, expanded, then the links. Escape returns to that button. FAQ category button announces General, current, and the others not current. A question button announces the question and collapsed. After Enter it announces expanded, and the next item is the answer region named by the question. Home and map combobox: the input announces Search stations, combobox, collapsed. After two characters the polite live region announces N results available or No matching stations without moving focus (4.1.3). Down Arrow announces the option name and selected. The option is a link with role=option; the name is the station, state, or ZIP, heard once. Escape announces collapsed. Use my location announces busy while the lookup runs. Map canvas: the virtual cursor hears the image name and the instruction to use search or Stations in view. A marker list inside the image is not expected. If Tab lands inside the map, note whether the attribution links are silent. That is a 4.1.2 failure while role=img stays on the Leaflet root. Stations in view announces N stations in view or No stations in view when the list updates (4.1.3). Map settings button announces Map settings, collapsed, then expanded, then the group Measurement filters and each checkbox name and checked state. Close settings is a button. Mobile search heading is Search stations, the close button is Close search, then the same combobox announcements. After Escape, the virtual cursor is back on the control that opened the overlay. Geolocation dialog: on open, the title and the body are read (aria-labelledby and aria-describedby) and focus is on OK. Titles from geolocation_errors.js are Location permission denied, Location request timed out, Location not supported, and Couldn't get your location. The permission-denied body says to allow location or search by name. Tab stays inside. Escape returns to Use my location. Contact: each field announces its label once; a placeholder, if heard, is a hint after the label. Required is announced. After an invalid submit the field announces invalid and the error text. Turnstile, if present, announces Bot check. The fallback link is Email hello@waterlevels.org. A base error uses role=alert and interrupts. Subscription: Email address, required, edit; button Email me a manage link. The alert flash interrupts. The success notice is polite and must be heard after the redirect (4.1.3). State directory (/gauges/wa): Search stations; groups Measurement types, Station status when any station is stale, and Flood alerts when any station is in flood. Each checkbox announces its label and checked state. After a change the live region says N stations shown or No stations match these filters, once. County headings are h2. On /alerts the same list announces Flood stages (Action Stage, Minor Flooding, Moderate Flooding, Major Flooding) and Measurement types, and the jump links are states. A flood card status line, on both pages, is the words Major Flooding, Minor Flooding, Moderate Flooding, Action Stage, Nominal, or Offline (1.4.1). Eyes-closed journeys: from / search a station and open it; from /map open settings and follow a station in view; from /alerts filter to a flood stage and open a card; from /gauges/wa filter by measurement type and open a card; submit /contact with a bad email and hear the error; request a manage link on /subscriptions.

CI. Add a fifth job, a11y, to .github/workflows/ci.yml. Keep scan_ruby, lint, javascript, and test. Same triggers: pull_request, and push to main. Runner ubuntu-latest. Steps follow the file already there: actions/checkout@v7, ruby/setup-ruby@v1 with bundler-cache, actions/setup-node@v7 with node-version-file .nvmrc (Node 24) and cache yarn, then yarn install --frozen-lockfile. Copy the postgres:16 and redis:7 service blocks from the test job, because gauge, state, and map pages read the database. Run bin/rails db:test:prepare and a small fixture load in RAILS_ENV=test so Turnstile is not required. Leave REDIS_URL unset, matching the comment on the test job. Install Chromium only (npx playwright install --with-deps chromium). Start Puma the way Procfile.dev does, bin/rails server -p 3000 -b 127.0.0.1, wait until http://127.0.0.1:3000 responds, then npx playwright test --project=a11y. There is no npm start script. Do not scan the public URL. Fail the job on any violation for those tags. Upload the Playwright report. Leave yarn test:js on the javascript job and the smoke test inside bin/rails test. Those already fail CI for banned contrast tokens and for missing skip links, landmarks, combobox attributes, FAQ button semantics, the mobile nav attributes, aria-current, contact error association, and gauge tabs. A green axe run is not a conformance claim. 2.4.11, 2.5.7, 3.2.6, 3.3.7, and 3.3.8 stay on the manual list. 2.5.8 is the WCAG 2.2 check the wcag22aa tag actually runs.
